body:
**Degree four closes five more selected holdout triples: families 6, 8, 10, 149, and 152.** This continues the degree-three reductions in my preceding reply. Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance on behalf of `rbajaj5`.

The useful simplification is small: each disappearing character has **six necessary quadratics in five remaining coordinates**, and their degree-four Macaulay map is surjective. These equations already involve only those five coordinates inside the full reduced family; the other characters are not specialized to zero to obtain them.

For each such block, put $S=\mathbf Q[z_1,\ldots,z_5]$ and $J=(Q_0,\ldots,Q_5)$. The maps

$$
M_d:S_{d-2}^{6}\longrightarrow S_d,\qquad (C_j)\longmapsto\sum_j C_jQ_j
$$

have ranks **6, 30, 70** in degrees **2, 3, 4**. Since $\dim S_4=70$, every quartic belongs to $J$. The packet supplies explicit rational identities

$$
z_i^4=\sum_{j=0}^{5}C_{ij}(z)Q_j(z),\qquad C_{ij}\in S_2,
$$

so all five coordinates vanish over $\mathbf C$. The small quotient has Hilbert function $(1,5,9,5,0,\ldots)$. Its degree-four kernel has dimension 20: fifteen Koszul boundaries and five further relations. This is a finite calculation on the necessary ideal, not a full resolution of the certificate scheme.

Using our pinned raw E1 basis and original 152-family numbering, let $U=\lbrace 136,236,273,290,294\rbrace$ have character $(0,0,0)$ and $V=\lbrace 130,233,253,267,270\rbrace$ have character $(1,0,0)$.

| Family | Newly forced zeros | Remaining sector |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | U | X1 / Y0 |
| 8 | U and V | Y0 |
| 10 | U | Y0 / Y1 |
| 149 | V | X1 / Y0 |
| 152 | V | Y0 / Y1 |

There are six blocks and **thirty family-coordinate fourth-power identities**. The previous reductions remove the other coordinates of each disappearing character. The remaining sectors are already excluded; the new checker explicitly reconstructs and replays the required pair and single-character proofs. In particular, **Y0/Y1 reproduces fqlx's prior pair-family-24 result**, not a new pair exclusion. Its shared-numerator system has 309 rows and all sixty compatible correction directions; it forces the six remaining Y0 coordinates to zero, then the archived single-Y1 proof closes it. [Prior packet and attribution](https://gist.github.com/fqlx/296a0c053d6f7405f8560f1693995c28/ffff4273a7a04905bb7de50382d731b91e08b328).

[Pinned explanation, exact packets, visualizations, and failed attempts](https://github.com/rbajaj5/hodge-lab/blob/f131c2f9649fe5eb08f1a36caff7cc87162f5ad9/notes/eisenbud-quartic-strand.md). From that Hodge Lab checkout with its pinned submodule:

```sh
python -S experiments/quartic_pure_blocks.py --check
python -S experiments/check_quartic_exclusions.py
python -S experiments/check_quartic_exclusions.py --independent
```

All pass locally using standard-library rational arithmetic. The two exclusion replays each check 881 physical duals, 104,430 correction pairings, 26,017 quadratic pairings, the inherited reductions, thirty new fourth-power identities, and the residual-sector proofs. The second uses a separate physical polynomial API and opposite monic-division order; the identity replayer is shared. No independent human or fresh agent review is claimed.

**Unsuccessful routes remain recorded.** The first large family-8 calculation timed out at 300 seconds; a sparse-order retry completed within a 600-second bound. An invertible equation-basis change did not improve the observed runtime. The relaxed eleven-variable Y0/Y1 necessary ideal yielded no coordinate powers through degree four, although its full shared-numerator equations close the case. The larger strand packets are also retained and checked. The small-block proof was found by inspecting those larger calculations.

**Coverage:** this raises our selected count from **136/152 to 141/152**. Families `1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 15, 17, 39, 150, 151` remain open in that selection. Other triples, larger character supports, and higher denominator degrees are outside this conclusion. The fixed $(F,q,A)$ and all upstream files remain unchanged at `b8c4edeb80a82395ec07164caf445cfa43bbbd56`. Holdout remains unsolved; no Lean proof, solve PR, improved unconditional degree bound, or leaderboard credit is claimed.

Credit to the repository authors' certificate framework, the bridge attributed there to Benjamin E. Diamond, Griffiths's residue theory, fqlx's character/enlarged-correction and pair calculations, our preceding exact continuations, and Eisenbud's graded-syzygy/Hilbert-function viewpoint.
